photo.title: A group of Kisii people encountered on the road,probably on the way to or from market. One woman is carrying a large basket and gourd on her head, and someone beyond has a large rolled mat of the type usually traded by the Luo into the Kisii market. [Gilbert Oteyo 9/9/2004]

A group of Kisii people encountered on the road, including women carrying baskets, children and men herding cattle. The clothing types seen here were not much practiced among the Luo, and is in keeping with styles of the time in the highlands among the Kipsigis, Nandi and Kisii. [Gilbert Oteyo 9/9/2004]

A group of women and children encountered on the road, described as a group of Kisii people. The women are carrying large baskets and pots on their heads. The clothing of overthrown-wrap as seen here was not much practiced among the Luo, as it was in the highlands among the Kipsigis, Nandi and Kisii. [Gilbert Oteyo 9/9/2004]

A group of young boys, girls and adults in the background encountered on the road, described as a group of Kisii people. One woman is carrying a large basket on her head. The clothing of overthrown-wrap as seen here with two of the men was not much practiced among the Luo, as it was in the highlands among the Kipsigis, Nandi and Kisii. [Gilbert Oteyo 9/9/2004]
A group of young boys, girls and adults in the background encountered on the road, described as a group of Kisii people. The women are carrying large baskets on their heads. [Gilbert Oteyo 9/9/2004]
A group of Kisii women and boys carrying large baskets and a large rolled mat of the type usually traded by the Luo into the Kisii market. [Gilbert Oteyo 9/9/2004]

This is a view of Mount Homa taken from Kendu Bay. Both the mountain and the lake shore township of Kendu Bay are in Karachuonyo Location of South Nyanza. The mountain is a major volcanic plug in the Lake Victoria Basin and is only a couple of kilometres from the lake. From the higher hills above Kendu Bay the land drops quickly into a low plain area and this leaves the mountain to stand out spectacularly. Mt. Home is associated with some hot springs, carbonate soda (bala) for medicine and cooking, and a number of Luo beliefs about their ancestors. In particular, there is a traditional belief about a big snake, known as Nyangoe, who is supposed to live there and who could cause hurricanes if not appeased. [Gilbert Oteyo 9/9/2004]

These people are listening to a musician playing a stringed instrument known as nyatiti. Whilst they are all wearing European clothing they have elements of Luo decoration, such as ostrich feather plumes (kondo udo) attached to their hats to mix styles. [Gilbert Oteyo 9/9/2004]
A man wearing a headdress decorated with leaves and shells.
